reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers, but duplicates non-working-day detection and daily skip policy across consumers.

duplication.why: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange independently implement the daily-skip versus move decision also embedded in getNextDate.

placement.why: Holiday matching belongs in shared/schedules.ts, but the server handlers also own scheduling policy that should live alongside those shared helpers.

scope.why: All edits directly support the requested scheduling rules, range handler, configuration field, or associated tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate three policy implementations and existing budget adjustment callers rather than update one shared occurrence policy.

bypasses_abstraction.where: In server/schedules/app.ts, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange spell out d.isWeekend(date) || isHoliday(...) instead of using isNonWorkingDay, and independently reproduce policy from shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate.

disguised_duplication.where: The flatMap callbacks in getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange reshape the same enabled/daily/non-working-day/adjustment decision using different nesting.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains holidays; getNextDate gains daily-specific filtering, residual rejection, and empty-result branches; the two server handlers implement their own skip-or-move policy and bypass isNonWorkingDay.
